To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellularly localized Al- and Znphtalocyanines (PcS4s) generate free radicals upon irradiation with visible light and that the radicals are involved in the photocytotoxicity of these compounds.
the phototoxicity and free-radical generation by tetrasulphonyl phthalocyanine photosensitisers are dependent on their pre-illumination incubations with cells.

the photoprocesses induced by tetrasulpho-phthalocyaninato metal complexes in lymphoma cells are mediated by the formation of free radicals, the nature and the yields of which depend on the incubation conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the phototoxicity mechanism of Al- and ZnPcS4 in lymphoma cells.
the elucidation of the photobiological properties of Al- and Zn-tetrasulphonated phthalocyanines and their use as potential phototherapeutic agents.
the photodynamic action of tetrasulphophthalocyanines in lymphoma cells, with particular emphasis on the intracellular generation of radicals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AlPcS(4) and ZnPc(S(4) are capable of producing free radicals and cytotoxicity in lymphoma cells and that these effects are related to the length of pre-illumination incubations with these photosensitizers.
Al- and ZnpPcS4 are capable of generating a variety of reactive oxygen species, including singlet oxygen and free radicals, which are able to damage cellular constituents and cause cell killing.
the photodynamic effects of MePcS are initiated by a free radical mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MePcS 4 are able to generate a variety of free radicals upon irradiation and that these radicals are responsible for the observed photodamage.
the phototoxicity induced by MePcSs is due to a free radical-mediated process and that the intracellularly generated radicals are derived from the MePcS and from cellular substrates.
the photocytotoxicity of Al- and Zn-phtalocyanine dyes is mediated by intracellular generation of oxygen radicals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AlPcS(4) and ZnPc(4) are capable of generating intracellular free radicals, which are responsible for their phototoxic effects.
the intracellular phototoxicity of MePcSs is a function of the length of the pre/post illumination incubation time.
the intracellular generation of DMPO/ox and DMPO/R, and to a lesser extent DMPO/OH, is a general phenomenon in cells exposed to MePcS.
